subtitle: Blood for ghosts: Tiresias, his mother, and the fallen at Troy

narrativeBlocks.title: To the edge of the world
narrativeBlocks.body: Circe's direction is unthinkable: the way home runs through Hades. Odysseus sails to the world's edge, digs a trench, and pours out sheep's blood — the price for the dead to speak.

narrativeBlocks.title: Tiresias's map home
narrativeBlocks.body: The blind prophet drinks and foretells: the journey can still succeed — if his men do not touch the Sun's cattle on Thrinacia. If they do, Odysseus will come home late, alone, on a foreign ship, to find trouble in his hall.

narrativeBlocks.title: His mother, dead of grief
narrativeBlocks.body: Among the shades is Anticleia — his own mother, dead while he wandered, of longing for him. He tries three times to hold her; she slips through his arms like smoke. The hero's greatest adventures are invisible to the people who paid for them.

narrativeBlocks.title: Achilles regrets
narrativeBlocks.body: The shade of Achilles delivers the epic's verdict on glory: better to be a living labourer under a poor man than king over all the dead. The anger-epic's hero, in the underworld, would trade his fame for an ordinary life.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why epics go underground
narrativeBlocks.body: Every great hero must eventually descend — Heracles, Theseus, Aeneas, Dante after them all. The underworld visit is where the story prices its own glory in the currency of the living.

quiz.prompt: Why does Circe send Odysseus to consult the dead?

choices.text: The dead prophet Tiresias alone can tell him how to reach home — and what will doom the voyage
He must retrieve a token of Hades as proof
His dead father demands an inheritance rite
The underworld holds the stolen Palladium

quiz.explanation: Tiresias's prophecy gives the route and the fatal condition: touch the Sun's cattle and all is lost.

quiz.prompt: What does Achilles's shade tell Odysseus about glory?

choices.text: He would rather be a poor living labourer than king of all the dead
That he regrets ever sailing to Troy
That death in battle brings the finest honour
That Patroclus waits for him beyond the river

quiz.explanation: The greatest hero of the Iliad values life over posthumous fame — the Odyssey's central counterweight to epic glory.
